name: Compass
tagline: Java search framework on Lucene with object-to-index mapping; Shay Banon's precursor to Elasticsearch.
description: Compass was an open-source Java framework that Shay Banon started in 2004 to make Apache Lucene usable as an application data store. Its core idea was OSEM, object/search engine mapping: annotate domain classes and Compass indexed them, kept the index in step with Hibernate, JPA and other ORM writes, and wrapped Lucene in transactional index operations, a query builder and XML or JSON mappings. It was widely used from Spring and Grails applications in the late 2000s. While designing Compass 3.0, Banon concluded that a scalable, distributed engine speaking JSON over HTTP needed a rewrite, released Elasticsearch in 2010, and announced that Compass 2.x was in maintenance mode and users should plan to migrate. The final line was 2.2.0, and the project site is offline.
statusNote: Superseded by Elasticsearch (2010); the author put Compass 2.x into maintenance and the project site is offline. Last line: 2.2.0.
strengths: Annotation-driven mapping from Java objects to a Lucene index
Kept search indexes in sync with Hibernate/JPA writes automatically
Transactional semantics over Lucene index updates
weaknesses: Discontinued since 2010 and tied to very old Lucene versions
Its author recommended migrating to Elasticsearch
useCases: Maintaining legacy Spring or Grails apps that still embed it
